construct: DES encodes desmin, the major muscle-specific cytoplasmic intermediate filament. Desmin links and mechanically integrates myofibrils with the sarcolemma and organelles; pathogenic DES variants can disrupt intermediate-filament assembly and cause skeletal myopathy, cardiomyopathy, and conduction disease.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: DES mutation plus desmin-positive aggregates, distal myopathy, conduction disease, and cardiomyopathy identifies desminopathy. Desmin is a muscle-specific intermediate-filament protein.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Actin and myosin are sarcomeric thin/thick filaments; tubulin forms microtubules; dystrophin is a membrane-associated actin-linking complex. None is the DES-encoded cytoskeletal class.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The direct DES genotype and desmin-positive aggregates make the intermediate-filament answer unique; difficulty is therefore correctly calibrated as easy.
